That prior fix (SYS-547, commits `6067fd46` + `c1f4f456`) took a third approach, different from either option I offered: **eliminate the redirect-with-query-param round-trip entirely** for that one flow.

Before: `/footy/auth/claim` page → redirected to an API route → which called `claimPlayerInvitation`, and on failure redirected back with `?error=<message>` in the URL, for a client component to read and display.

After: `src/app/footy/auth/claim/[token]/page.tsx` became a Server Component that calls `claimPlayerInvitation(token)` directly, in a `try/catch`, during render — no route, no redirect, no query param at all. The error message is computed fresh server-side on every request and passed straight into JSX as a prop, so it can never be attacker-supplied via a crafted URL, and there's nothing to sanitize because the value never touches the URL.

That pattern maps cleanly onto **`src/app/footy/response/[token]/route.ts`**: it also exists purely to compute something server-side and hand it to a page, and its errors (`Missing token.`, `Invitation not found.`) are fully known application strings, not user input — so `src/app/footy/response/page.tsx` could just call `getGameInvitationResponseDetails` directly instead of going through a route that redirects with `?error=`.

It maps less cleanly onto the other two:
- **`src/app/api/footy/auth/claim/[token]/route.ts`** (the *finalize*-signup step, still live — `ClaimSignup.tsx:59` redirects to it) — this one redirects to an arbitrary caller-supplied `redirectParam` (e.g. `/footy/profile`) on completion, not back to itself, so there's no single page to inline the logic into.
- **`src/app/api/footy/auth/verify/[purpose]/[token]/route.ts`** — same shape: it's an email-link target that redirects onward to `redirectParam`, shared across `extra-email` and `enquiry` purposes.

For those two, a closed enum of reason codes (my original option 1) is the natural fit, since they genuinely need to carry a signal across a redirect to a different page.

Want me to proceed with: **inline server-side logic** for the response route/page (matching the SYS-547 precedent), and a **closed enum of reason codes** for the claim-finalize and verify routes (removing `SearchParamErrorNotification`'s raw-text rendering and `EnquiryForm`'s redundant reader in favour of it)?

# SYS-590: Stop rendering `?error=` as trusted display text

## Context

`SearchParamErrorNotification` (mounted globally in `src/app/footy/layout.tsx`) reads `searchParams.get('error')` and renders it verbatim as a red "Error" toast on every page under `/footy/**`. Because it doesn't care where the value came from, a crafted URL like `https://www.toastboy.co.uk/footy/anything?error=<phishing text>` renders attacker-authored text as a legitimate-looking app error — a ready-made phishing primitive.

Investigation found three producers that redirect with `?error=<message>` (`auth/claim/[token]/route.ts`, `auth/verify/[purpose]/[token]/route.ts`, `api/footy/response/[token]/route.ts`) and three consumers that render it as trusted text (`SearchParamErrorNotification`, `EnquiryForm`'s own redundant reader, and `footy/response/page.tsx`'s inline `<Text>{errorMessage}</Text>`). A fourth, previously unflagged instance of the same idiom was also found: `footy/(authenticated)/profile/page.tsx` reads `purpose`/`email` query params and — regardless of whether any producer currently sets them (none do; this is dead code today) — passes `email` straight into `PlayerProfileForm`, which shows a teal "Email verified" toast containing that raw text. This is live and exploitable right now via `/footy/profile?purpose=player_email&email=<anything>`, independent of the `error` param. It falls under acceptance criterion 4 ("no remaining code path renders a raw searchParams value directly into UI") and gets fixed for free once the producer that *should* set it is redesigned.

A prior fix for the `player-invite` flow (SYS-547, commits `6067fd46`/`c1f4f456`) established the precedent this plan follows: rather than redirecting through an API route that appends a message to the URL, make the destination itself a Server Component page that performs the action server-side (in a `try/catch`) and renders the outcome directly as a prop — no query param ever carries free text. That works because `finalizePlayerInvitationClaim`/`verifyEmail`/`deliverContactEnquiry`/`getGameInvitationResponseDetails` errors already carry a safe, developer-authored `publicMessage` (via `AppError`/`toPublicMessage`) — the vulnerability was never the message content, only the fact that the consumer trusted whatever text sat in the URL regardless of provenance.

Checking actual call sites confirmed every `redirect` target in the app is a single hardcoded literal per flow (never derived from user input): claim-finalize and extra-email verification both always go to `/footy/profile`; the enquiry verification always goes to `/footy/info` today. That means every one of the three remaining redirect-based flows can drop the query-param mechanism entirely and adopt the SYS-547 pattern, rather than needing a closed-enum scheme.

## Approach, flow by flow

### 1. Game invitation response (`api/footy/response/[token]/route.ts`)
`footy/response/page.tsx` already ignores every flattened query param except `token` and re-fetches via `getGameInvitationResponseDetails(token)` itself — the route is already redundant for the success path. Simplify:
- Change the invite link in `src/lib/gameInvitations.ts:128` from `/api/footy/response/${token}` to `/footy/response?token=${token}`.
- In `footy/response/page.tsx`, drop the `error` search param entirely. Keep the existing `redirect('/footy/game')` for the no-token case. When `getGameInvitationResponseDetails(token)` returns `null`, render the existing inline "Invitation details are missing." message (already there) instead of a separate `?error=Invitation not found.` case — same UX, one fewer code path.
- Delete `src/app/api/footy/response/[token]/route.ts` and its spec.
- `revalidatePath('/footy/response')` call sites (`submitResponse.ts`, `triggerInvitations.ts`, `submitGameInvitationResponse.ts`, `api/footy/invitations/route.ts`) are unaffected — the page URL doesn't change shape.

### 2. Player-invitation claim finalize (`api/footy/auth/claim/[token]/route.ts`)
This route is reached two ways: `ClaimSignup.tsx`'s `router.push` after email/password signup, and as the OAuth callback URL for Google/Microsoft sign-in (`socialRedirect`) — both are just a GET to a URL, so a page works for either.
- New page `src/app/footy/auth/claim/[token]/finish/page.tsx`: call the existing `finalizePlayerInvitationClaim` action in a `try/catch`. On success, `redirect('/footy/profile')` (from `next/navigation`, same pattern already used in `footy/response/page.tsx`). On failure, compute the message with `toPublicMessage` (same pattern as the existing `footy/auth/claim/[token]/page.tsx`) and render it inline via `Notification`, with an `Anchor` back to `/footy/profile` or `/footy`.
- Update `ClaimSignup.tsx`: `redirectPath`/`socialRedirect` become `/footy/auth/claim/${token}/finish` — no `?redirect=` param.
- Delete `src/app/api/footy/auth/claim/[token]/route.ts` and its spec.

In general, what should be the determining factor for using search params rather than path segments? In cases where there are lots of optional params (where the existence of one doesn't necessarily assume the existence of any given other) then I think searchParams are the only way to go, but in cases like password reset where there's only ever one, and it's required, should that be a path segment?

Two independent factors, and either alone can force the decision:

**1. Cardinality/optionality** — your instinct is right. If a value is required and there's exactly one of it, it belongs in the path; it's part of what makes this URL "this specific thing" rather than a variant of a shared page. Path segments in frameworks like Next.js also don't compose well for many independent optionals (you end up with catch-all segments and manual parsing), so once you have several orthogonal optional values, query params are the only ergonomic choice.

**2. Sensitivity** — independent of cardinality, anything bearer-style (a secret that alone grants access — session tokens, password-reset tokens, invitation tokens, API keys) should avoid query strings regardless of how many params there are, because query strings leak through channels path segments mostly don't: Referer headers on outbound navigation, proxy/CDN/server access logs that capture full request URLs, browser history and autocomplete, and analytics tools that record full page URLs by default. A single required param that happens to be sensitive should go in the path even if it were the *only* thing that would tempt you toward query-string simplicity.

Password reset is exactly the case where both factors agree: one required value, and it's a bearer credential. It should be a path segment (`/reset-password/[token]`), same as the invitation/verification tokens we just moved in this session.

The useful split in practice: path segments answer "which resource/instance is this," query params answer "how do I want to view/filter/paginate it, or what should happen after." `redirect=`, `sort=`, `tab=`, pagination cursors — genuinely optional, non-identifying, non-sensitive — stay in the query string. Anything that's *required to make the URL mean something*, or that alone would let someone act as another user if intercepted, goes in the path.

Full audit of every `searchParams` usage in the codebase (9 pages, 1 client hook, 1 API route) — no changes made, per your instruction.

## Should become a path segment — sensitivity-driven

**`src/app/footy/auth/reset-password/page.tsx`** — `token` is required (page shows an error if it's missing) and it's a bearer-style credential: whoever holds it can set that account's password. Same category as the invitation/verification tokens fixed under SYS-590 — should be `/footy/auth/reset-password/[token]`.

Caveat: this link isn't built by our code. `ForgottenPasswordForm.tsx` calls Better Auth's `authClient.requestPasswordReset({ email, redirectTo })` — Better Auth constructs the actual token URL and appends `token` as a query param when it redirects the user to `redirectTo` after they click the emailed link. Changing this would mean checking whether Better Auth supports a path-segment-shaped reset URL at all, not just editing our own route — a different kind of fix from the others.

## Should become a path segment — cardinality/canonical-URL-driven (no security angle)

Six pages share an identical pattern for a `year` search param: it's required in practice (404s if missing/invalid — it isn't a real optional filter with a graceful default), and each page already computes a "canonical URL" and does a `permanentRedirect()` if the current URL doesn't match it:

- `src/app/footy/books/page.tsx`
- `src/app/footy/curse/page.tsx`
- `src/app/footy/games/page.tsx`
- `src/app/footy/winners/page.tsx`
- `src/app/footy/table/[table]/page.tsx` — already has one required path segment (`table`); `year` is a second one bolted on as a query param instead of joining it
- `src/app/footy/player/[id]/page.tsx` — same shape, `id` is a path segment, `year` isn't

This is the general form of what you described: required, singular, and it *identifies which version of the page you're on* enough that the app enforces one canonical URL for it — that's a path segment by the same logic as an identifying resource ID, just without the sensitivity angle. Structurally these look like `/footy/table/[table]/[year]`, `/footy/winners/[year]`, `/footy/player/[id]/[year]`, etc.

All six route through one shared component, `src/components/TitleWithYearDropdown/TitleWithYearDropdown.tsx`, which builds the `?year=` links via `useSearchParams`/`usePathname`. That's the single choke point that would need to become path-template-aware (it'd need to know each page's URL shape rather than just rewriting the current pathname's query string), so this is a bigger, more coupled change than the token fixes were.

## Borderline — low priority

**`src/app/api/events/route.ts`** — `?channel=<name>` for the SSE subscription (`useAutoRefresh.ts`). Required and singular, but not sensitive (a small closed enum of channel names, not a secret) and query params are conventional for `EventSource`/stream endpoints. Defensible as-is; I wouldn't prioritize this one.

## Correctly query params — no change warranted

- **`src/app/footy/auth/signin/page.tsx`** (`redirect`, `admin`) — optional, non-identifying view modifiers, exactly the case for query params.
- **`src/app/footy/admin/invoice/page.tsx`** (`year`, `month`) — optional with a sensible default (next month), no canonical-URL enforcement, no 404 on absence. Genuinely optional, unlike the six pages above.
